- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast for next 5 days at 1–2% below peak.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish — adjust downward by 1–2% for short-term (1–3 day) forecasts.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates mean price; apply a 1–3% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or bearish in recent 7 days.
- If sentiment is high and price is near historical mean, model tends to overreact — dampen forecast by 1–3% for 10–30 day horizon.
